claims.text: Equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi is an example of the high-entropy alloys fabricated by L-PBF in the proposed application.
HEA components produced under standard L-PBF conditions currently exhibit dimensional inaccuracies.
HEA components produced under standard L-PBF conditions currently exhibit non-uniform microstructures.
L-PBF fabrication of CoCrFeMnNi can involve porosity and keyholing defects.
The proposed intervention is an in situ closed-loop machine-learning system using high-speed imaging and pyrometry to adjust laser power, scan speed, and beam path during a build.
Standard L-PBF processing of HEAs is characterized by rapid solidification, high thermal gradients, and layer-wise deposition.
Real-time adjustment of laser power and scan speed will adaptively modulate melt-pool dynamics.
Adaptive laser-parameter modulation will stabilize melt-pool geometry.
Adaptive laser-parameter modulation will control thermal gradients.
The machine-learning system can use real-time sensor data to predict potential defect formation.
Immediate tuning of laser parameters will minimize localized overheating.
Immediate tuning of laser parameters will reduce thermal stresses.
Closed-loop parameter control will promote a more uniform microstructure.
Compared with static parameter settings, ML-enabled control will significantly reduce dimensional deviations.
Compared with static parameter settings, ML-enabled control will improve tensile strength and ductility.
Compared with static parameter settings, ML-enabled control will lower the density of process-induced defects.
Current static-parameter HEA processes produce inconsistent melt-pool behavior, higher defect densities, and dimensional imprecision.
Sensor resolution, control-response lag, and monitoring disruption under extreme processing conditions can limit intervention effectiveness.
Closed-loop control performance may be alloy-dependent and require separate calibration for different HEA compositions.
Failure to obtain statistically significant improvements in dimensional precision, tensile performance, and defect reduction relative to a static-parameter control would falsify the hypothesis.
